title: Egress rate limiter policy orphaning causing cross-environment outage
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Several customers reported 429/timeout cascades across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments starting 2026-03-09 21:40 UTC. Root cause analysis shows a control-plane -> data-plane policy sync regression: egress rate-limiter objects were occasionally created without an active 'burstAllowance' provenance field (TTL metadata), which caused the runtime to treat those policies as 'orphaned' and apply a conservative fallback enforcement (drop-to-1req/s). The fallback path is intended as a safety net for unknown policy states but was accidentally applied for valid policies when policy-version metadata was missing during a rolling control-plane upgrade. This manifested as widespread severe throttling for long-running customers and bursty workloads (webhooks, streaming responses).

Impact: Customers on Hosted (multi-tenant), Dedicated pools with mixed control-plane versions, and Private instances that performed a semi-automated control-plane upgrade experienced degraded throughput and API errors. Several enterprise customers escalated through CSMs and SRE due to production outages and missed SLAs. The outage affected both short-term latency-sensitive traffic and longer streaming token flows.

Why this happened: A schema change (policy_metadata.v2) was introduced in runtime-2.4 to add a "provenance"/"burstAllowance_ttl" field to rate-limit objects. The rollout included a control-plane migration that wrote policies with and without the new field during a 15-minute dual-write window. The data-plane policy loader had a strict validation that rejected policies missing the field; reject logic was wrapped under an error-handling path that sets enforcement to the conservative fallback. Under high load during the rollout, several in-flight updates lost the field due to non-atomic migration writes. Additionally, Dedicated autoscaler reconcilers retried writes and occasionally created duplicate policy IDs missing new metadata. Private customers who ran the semi-automated upgrade script with an earlier CL of the control plane saw the same orphaning pattern.

Immediate mitigations taken: 1) Rolled back the control-plane migration within 12 minutes of detection to stop new malformed policies from being emitted. 2) Deployed a hotfix to the data-plane policy loader that treats missing provenance as 'compatibility mode' (accept and backfill) instead of flipping to conservative enforcement. Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2409. 3) For affected Dedicated pools we triggered a policy reconcile job (reapply canonical policies) and restarted a small subset of workers to pick up corrected policy blobs. 4) For Private customers we delivered a one-click remediation script and coordinated hand-offs with Solutions Eng.

Planned permanent fix: 1) Add schema-tolerant migration in control-plane: write both v1 and v2 fields atomically and emit a verification event upon success. 2) Data-plane policy loader: implement a reconciliation pass that queries the canonical policy store and backfills missing metadata on startup, and add stricter invariants only after a safe migration window. 3) Add end-to-end test harness that simulates dual-write windows, network partial failures, and Dedicated autoscaler retries to catch similar regressions. 4) Add telemetry: metric policy_load_malformed_count and a per-customer throttling alert when fallback-enforcement is applied.

Customer communications: We sent incident summaries to affected customers (template link: https://docs.redwood.ai/incident-templates/rl-policy-outage) and are offering dedicated postmortem sessions for enterprise accounts. CSMs are coordinating credits where SLAs were missed.

Longer-term follow-ups (postmortem action items): schedule a migration playbook for future schema changes, add canary gating by policy-load metrics, and harden Dedicated reconciler idempotency.

Attachments/References: incident channel #incident-2026-03-09, PI dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/rl-outage, hotfix PR and cherry-picks for runtime-2.4.1, customer escalation tracker Google Sheet.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy control-plane migration that writes policy_metadata.v2 while some nodes remain on v1 -> observe dual-write window
Under high write load (>=200 policy updates/min), cause a few policy writes to truncate 'burstAllowance_ttl' field via a simulated partial write
Restart data-plane policy loader on a worker running runtime-2.4 and observe that malformed policy triggers fallback enforcement path
Send burst traffic to an endpoint that relies on policy-based burstAllowance and observe dropped requests / 429s when fallback enforcement applies
acceptance_criteria: Control-plane migration writes are atomic or emit verification event; schema-compat dual-write implemented
Data-plane no longer flips to conservative fallback solely due to missing provenance; malformed count metric near zero for 72h post-release
E2E test reproducer added to CI and documented playbook exists
Affected customers confirmed restored throughput and received postmortem follow-up
notes: Timeline: 2026-03-09 21:38 UTC first alerts from Grafana -> 21:46 rollback completed -> 22:05 hotfix staged -> 22:28 majority of traffic recovered
Related work: ENG-12555 (Dedicated reconciler idempotency) and ENG-12421 (policy-schema-migrations)
Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2409 (merged to main, cherrypick to runtime-2.4.1)
Customer contacts: AcmeHealth, Finlytics, CloudForms (CSMs notified)
Docs: incident template and remediation scripts in /docs/incidents/rl-policy-orphaning.md
